name: How a Paper Is Cited
title: How a Paper Is Cited
answer: How a paper is cited covers the ways a research work is referenced, counted, and traced across the literature. It includes direct citations, co-citations, bibliographic coupling, and citation contexts, not just raw counts. For a working researcher, this means understanding which later papers build on a claim, which earlier papers a work depends on, and where a citation is supportive, critical, or perfunctory. The site treats a citation as a link to the original paper, never to an aggregator.

sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: Citation mapping runs on a structured library of research papers, extracted claims, and model and tool records. The site currently holds 135 research papers, 10,555 extracted claims, 91 AI books, 801 scientific models, 732 AI tools, and 674 glossary terms. These records are indexed so that a paper's reference list and the papers that cite it can be resolved against the original source. No external search tool is used for citation links.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work is done by parsing reference lists and in-text citation markers, then matching each cited work to a canonical record. Claims extracted from research works are tied to the papers that make them, so a citation can be followed from a claim to the paper and then to later papers that cite it. Citation context is read to distinguish a paper that is merely mentioned from one whose method or result is actually used. The output is a map of influence and dependence, not a popularity score.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk in citation mapping center on provenance and misattribution. A citation must resolve to the original paper, and the site's content never links to the Consensus search tool; it links to the original paper. This reduces the risk of a reader landing on a summary or a gated third-party page instead of the source. The main risks are incomplete reference parsing, ambiguous author names, and preprint version drift, so records are kept against the version that was actually cited.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Citation mapping is moving toward context-aware citation graphs that show not just who cites whom but why. As extracted claims become more structured, a reader will be able to see which specific claim in a paper is supported or challenged by a later citation. The site's growing library of papers, claims, models, and tools points toward a research map where a citation is a typed edge with a reason attached. The likely next step is automated detection of citation intent at scale, without replacing the original paper as the destination.
